questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Rise of Chhatrapati Shivaji' refers to.
questions.a: Chhatrapati Shivaji carved an independent Maratha kingdom out of the Deccan in the seventeenth century by seizing hill forts, building a disciplined army and navy, and crowning himself sovereign king in 1674, challenging the might of the Adil Shahi sultans and the Mughals.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rise of Chhatrapati Shivaji'.
questions.a: Hill forts, swift cavalry and clever diplomacy built a Maratha state under Shivaji.

concepts.title: Shivaji's Administration and the Sovereign King

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Shivaji's Administration and the Sovereign King' refers to.
questions.a: Shivaji ran his kingdom through an organised council of eight ministers, collected fair taxes, kept his forces disciplined even inside enemy territory, and styled himself a sovereign king serving his people - the famous royal ideal recorded in his counsel to his son.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Shivaji's Administration and the Sovereign King'.
questions.a: A council of ministers, fair revenue and people-first rule made the Maratha state durable.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Shivaji's Administration and the Sovereign King' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3 (source: hees103.txt lines 552-806 (the sovereign king, counsel and administration))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Marathas after Shivaji' refers to.
questions.a: After Shivaji's death his son Sambhaji and successors carried the struggle against Mughal expansion; under the Peshwas in the eighteenth century the Maratha confederacy of houses like Scindia, Holkar, Gaekwad and Bhonsle spread Maratha influence across most of India.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Marathas after Shivaji'.
questions.a: From a Deccan kingdom to an all-India confederacy - Maratha power kept growing after 1680.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Marathas after Shivaji' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3 (source: hees103.txt lines 423-550 (the Marathas after Chhatrapati Shivaji))

concepts.title: Maratha Legacy and centres like Thanjavur

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Maratha Legacy and centres like Thanjavur' refers to.
questions.a: The Marathas left a lasting legacy in administration, military organisation and culture - patronising temples and learning, and ruling centres such as Thanjavur, where Maratha kings supported art, music and scholarship well into the colonial era.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Maratha Legacy and centres like Thanjavur'.
questions.a: Maratha rule shaped polity and culture alike, from hill forts to Thanjavur's courts.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Maratha Legacy and centres like Thanjavur' taught, and from which source text?
